112:       } else if (pos >= sentenceStarts[currentSentence + 1]) {
113:         int newMinSentence = currentSentence + 1;
114:         currentSentence = maxSentence - (maxSentence - currentSentence) / 2;
115:         moveToSentenceAt(pos, newMinSentence, maxSentence);
116:       }
117:     } else {
118:       assert currentSentence == minSentence;

The one-line change in `lucene/analysis/opennlp/src/java/org/apache/lucene/analysis/opennlp/OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator.java:160` corrects the "start search from the middle" computation in `preceding(int)` from `sentenceStarts.length / 2` to `(sentenceStarts.length - 1) / 2`, matching the pattern already used in `following(int)`.

Validation (Gradle couldn't run in the container — no network, no cached distribution/jars — so I verified with a standalone replica of the exact iterator logic):
- Buggy version reproduces `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 2 out of bounds for length 2` at the `preceding(25)` scenario from `TestOpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator.testPrecedingWithTwoSentences`
- Fixed version returns `0` as the test expects, and also passes the existing three-sentence, single-sentence, zero-sentence, and slice scenarios from the test file
- A fuzz run (2000 trials, 1–5 sentences, every offset via `preceding`/`following`) completes without exceptions
